newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY'S CENTRAL BANK RELIEVES RUN-HIT POSTABANK.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY'S CENTRAL BANK RELIEVES RUN-HIT POSTABANK.

text.p: The National Bank of Hungary (NBH) granted a one-month exemption from the placing of obligatory reserves with the NBH, to Postabank Rt, which was hit by panic withdrawals recently, the daily Nepszabadsag said.
Quoting unnamed sources, Nepszabadsag said that the exemption to Postabank, Hungary's second largest commercial bank, is valid until April 15.

The NBH declined to confirm Mepszabadsag's information on Thursday, but NBH officials said that central bank chairman Gyorgy Suranyi was likely to respond at a news conference, to be held on Friday, at 0800 GMT.
Nepszabadsag added that with the move the NBH aimed at preserving the liquidity of the interbank market, where Postabank is usually a large lender.
The exemption frees some 20 billion forints at the bank, from which depositors withdrew around 24 billion forints three weeks ago in a four-day-long rumour-triggered panic wave.
The daily also said that SBC Warburg, on behalf of Postabank, continued negotiations with foreign investors about a capital increase at Postabank.

The daily said that Bank Austria would be interested in acquiring a stake above 50 percent in Postabank, but the Hungarian bank's managers would prefer two or three investors which would each buy a maximum 15 percent stake.
Nepszabadsag added that Far East and Irish banks have already expressed interest in buying into Postabank.
